THE SPLIT PLATE / RECIPE

High-Protein Taco Bowls

Quest Loaded Taco chips as the bowl base = chips that contribute 19g protein instead of zero. Plus 93/7 lean beef + Kraft fat-free cheddar + a 1 tbsp bone-broth moisture hack per meal-prep container ≈ 61g protein per adult at 500 cal (estimated). The kid plate strips out the macro tricks (Velveeta, regular chips, full mini guac) — same flavor, no friction.

YIELD4 servings
TOTAL TIME20 min
COOK METHODSee method
EST. / SERVING~500 cal | ~61g protein
KEY TO SUCCESS: TWO PHASES: SEASON + BROWN → BRAISE + MELT. Phase 1 = brown the seasoned beef until just cooked through (6-8 min). Phase 2 = pour 1/3 cup Kirkland Sipping Bone Broth into the pan, reduce 60 sec, then add cheese to melt. Phase 2 is the texture unlock — never skip the broth step.

Ingredients

PROTEIN

  • 1.25 lb (20 oz) 93/7 lean ground beef
  • 2 tbsp Spiceology Taco Seasoning Blend
  • Pinch kosher salt

ADULT BASE

  • 2 bags Quest Loaded Taco Tortilla-Style Protein Chips (1 per adult bowl, 1.1 oz each)

ADULT CHEESE

  • 2 oz Kraft Fat-Free Shredded Cheddar (1 oz per plate)

Option 1

  • Simply Tostitos Organic Yellow Corn Tortilla Chips (~1 oz per kid)
  • 1 oz Tillamook Medium Cheddar (0.5 oz per plate)
  • 1 compartment kid tray per child (4-section tray, like EZPZ Happy Mat)
  • Small side bowl for lettuce + tomato

Option 3

  • Simply Tostitos Organic Yellow Corn Tortilla Chips (~1 oz per kid)
  • 1 oz Tillamook Medium Cheddar (0.5 oz per plate)
  • 1 compartment kid tray per child (4-section tray, like EZPZ Happy Mat)
  • Small side bowl for lettuce + tomato

BRAISE

  • 1/3 cup Kirkland Organic Chicken Sipping Bone Broth

TOPPING SHARED

  • 1 head iceberg lettuce, shredded (~3 cups)
  • 2 Roma tomatoes, diced
  • Pinch salt
  • 4 Wholly Guacamole Classic Minis (1 per plate)
  • Cooking spray (Chosen Foods avocado oil)

ADULT FORMAT

  • 1 wide white bowl per adult

Option 2

  • Simply Tostitos Organic Yellow Corn Tortilla Chips (~1 oz per kid)
  • 1 oz Tillamook Medium Cheddar (0.5 oz per plate)
  • 1 compartment kid tray per child (4-section tray, like EZPZ Happy Mat)
  • Small side bowl for lettuce + tomato

Allergens: dairy.

AT THE PAN — CHEESE SPLIT BY ZONE. Same Spiceology-seasoned beef + same Kirkland bone broth braise for everyone. The split is: (1) the cheese — Kraft fat-free for adult zone, Tillamook Medium for kid zone; (2) the chip — Quest Loaded Taco for adults (bowl base), Simply Tostitos Organic for kids (compartment); (3) the format — adult bowl (assembled), kid compartment tray (build-your-own at the table).

Method

Shared base

  1. 1.MISE. Spiceology Taco Seasoning out, 1.25 lb 93/7 beef in a stainless mixing bowl, Quest Loaded Taco chips bags out (2), Simply Tostitos Organic for kids, Kraft fat-free cheddar + Tillamook Medium cheddar shredded, 4 Wholly Guacamole minis, iceberg + Roma tomatoes ready, Kirkland Sipping Bone Broth pouch open.
  2. 2.SEASON BEEF. 1.25 lb beef into the stainless mixing bowl. Add 2 tbsp Spiceology Taco Seasoning Blend + pinch of kosher salt. Mix with hands or a spatula until the seasoning is evenly distributed (1-2 min).
  3. 3.DICE + SHRED. 2 Roma tomatoes diced ~1/4-inch. 1 head iceberg shredded thin (~3 cups). Combine in a small bowl with a pinch of salt. Set aside.
  4. 4.BROWN BEEF. Stainless skillet over medium-high. Cooking spray. Seasoned beef in. Break up as it browns, 6-8 min until just cooked through. 93/7 is lean enough that you don't need to drain.
  5. 5.BONE BROTH BRAISE. Pour 1/3 cup Kirkland Sipping Bone Broth into the beef. Reduce 60 sec on medium-high — the broth carries the seasoning back into the meat. THIS STEP IS NON-NEGOTIABLE for the cheese melt + flavor distribution.
  6. 6.CHEESE SPLIT BY ZONE. Push beef into two zones. ~70% adult-side: sprinkle 2 oz Kraft Fat-Free Shredded Cheddar. ~30% kid-side: sprinkle 1 oz Tillamook Medium Cheddar. Cover 60 sec. Cheese melts under the lid.

Adult — Quest Chips Bowl + Fat-Free Cheddar Beef + Wholly + Iceberg/Roma

  1. 7.ADULT BOWL. Empty 1 bag Quest Loaded Taco chips into the bottom of a wide white bowl. Light crush with the back of a spoon (keep half-chips for texture). Spoon ~6 oz of the cheesy fat-free-cheddar beef from the adult zone over the chips.
  2. 8.TOP THE ADULT BOWL. Scatter ~1 cup shredded iceberg + diced Roma tomato over the beef. Squeeze 1 Wholly Guacamole Classic Mini in the center as a dollop. Optional: hot sauce on the side (Lucky Dog, Cholula). Eat with a spoon, scoop through all layers.

Kid — Compartment Tray (Build-Your-Own, Tostitos + Medium Cheddar) · Option 1

  1. 7.KID TRAY. Compartment tray. Large compartment: ~1 oz Simply Tostitos Organic Yellow Corn chips (about 10-12 chips). Small compartment 1: 3 oz of the medium-cheddar kid-zone beef. Small compartment 2: 1 Wholly Guacamole Classic Mini squeezed in. Side bowl: small portion of lettuce + Roma tomato mix.
  2. 8.ASSEMBLY (kid leads). Chip + dab of beef + scoop of guac = bite. Some kids dip the chip into the guac directly + chase with a beef bite. Either pattern works. Don't pre-assemble nachos for them — the chips go soggy in 30 sec.

Kid — Compartment Tray (Build-Your-Own, Tostitos + Medium Cheddar) · Option 2

  1. 7.1 small flour tortilla + 0.5 oz cheddar + 3 oz cheesy beef. Fold in half. Skillet over medium 90 sec/side until the cheese melts + the tortilla browns. Cut into 4 wedges. Wholly mini becomes the dip on the side.

Kid — Compartment Tray (Build-Your-Own, Tostitos + Medium Cheddar) · Option 3

  1. 7.Regular kid plate. 3 oz of cheesy beef in one corner, ~10 Tostitos in another, Wholly mini dollop separately, lettuce/tomato in a small side bowl. No assembly expectation — kid can eat the beef plain with a spoon if they want.

SPLIT PLATE SERVING

Adult — Quest Chips Bowl + Fat-Free Cheddar Beef + Wholly + Iceberg/Roma: Serve the adult portion as described above.

Kid — Compartment Tray (Build-Your-Own, Tostitos + Medium Cheddar): Serve the kid portion as described above.

Keys to success

  • 93/7 BEEF — NO FAT DRAIN. The leanness profile barely produces visible rendered fat. Skip the drain step entirely. If you used 80/20 or 85/15, drain it; but the recipe is built on 93/7 and the drain isn't needed.
  • 2 TBSP SPICEOLOGY PER 1.25 LB BEEF. Measured, not eyeballed. The salt-forward blend gets bitter past 2.5 tbsp.

If something fails

Cheese seized into rubbery flecks instead of melting: You skipped the bone-broth braise step. Fat-free cheddar needs moisture to melt. Add 2 tbsp more bone broth, stir over LOW heat 30 sec, the cheese will smooth out.

Beef tastes dry / over-seasoned crust on the outside, no flavor inside: Same root cause — you skipped the bone-broth step. The broth carries the dry seasoning back into the meat. Pour 1/3 cup into the cooked beef, reduce 60 sec, THEN cheese.

Quest chips went soft / soggy by the second bite: Either the beef was too hot when it hit the chips (let it sit 60 sec off heat first) or you used too much beef-juice for the chip-to-beef ratio. Reduce the broth further before saucing the chips, or just plate chips in a smaller portion + add more chips during eating.

Kid wouldn't touch the Tostitos but ate the beef: Expected first time with the compartment-tray format. Hold the line — components are the same, kid will mix/match by night 2-3. Or swap kid chips to whatever they currently eat (Doritos, Goldfish, plain crackers) if you want zero negotiation.

Macros came in higher than 500 cal/adult: Most likely cause: (1) used 80/20 beef instead of 93/7 (adds ~100 cal), (2) used full-fat sharp cheddar instead of Kraft fat-free (adds ~65 cal), or (3) ate more than 1 bag of Quest chips. The 500-cal budget is tight — skip ANY of the macro levers and you climb 65-100 cal.

Adult bowl looks anemic / lacks restaurant signal: Plate composition matters here. White wide bowl > cereal bowl. Chips spread to fill the bottom; beef in a generous mound center; lettuce + tomato around the edges; guac dollop on top center. Hot sauce bottle on the side as the visual accent (Lucky Dog, Cholula, whatever).

Storage and reheating

Store: MEAL-PREP FIRST DESIGN. Cook 2 lb beef once, divide evenly into 6 airtight meal-prep containers. Splash 1 tbsp Kirkland Sipping Bone Broth over each container (moisture hack). Add cheese to each container — 1 oz Kraft Fat-Free Cheddar to adult containers, 1.5 Velveeta slices to shared kid containers. Refrigerate up to 4 days. Store chopped romaine + halved yellow cherry tomatoes SEPARATELY (3-4 days). Keep chips in sealed bags at room temperature and assemble only when eating.

Reheat: Beef container: microwave ~90 sec covered, until hot. The 1 tbsp bone broth splash keeps the beef moist through the reheat and helps the fat-free cheddar melt cleanly (or the Velveeta on the kid side). Chips: serve room temperature — DON'T microwave. Produce: never reheat (wilts). Don't pre-assemble + store — the chips go soggy in 30 minutes flat.

Lasts: Cooked beef holds up to 4 days in the fridge, freezes 2 months. Quest chips: sealed bag at room temp 3-4 weeks. Simply Tostitos: sealed bag 4-6 weeks. Chopped romaine + yellow cherry tomatoes: 2-3 days max. Wholly minis: per package date. The refresh is meal-prep-first — cook once, portion into 6 containers, assemble each meal fresh.

Estimated nutrition

~500 cal | ~61g protein.

Brands I use

93/7 Lean Ground Beef
2 lb pack — batches into 6 adult-equivalent servings (~5 1/3 oz raw-equivalent per adult, ~227 cal / 31g protein per portion)
The macro architecture is built on the leanness — 93/7 lets the bowl carry full-fat-equivalent cheddar and guacamole without exceeding the 500-cal budget. 80/20 adds ~100 cal per plate and breaks the high-protein/low-fat lane. The drain step isn't needed.
Dan-O's
TAC-O Seasoning (salt-forward taco blend — filmed in the refresh)
Filmed in the 2026-08-28 refresh as the taco flavor anchor. Salt-forward taco blend with cumin + smoked paprika + chili. Sub Spiceology Taco Seasoning or homemade — same effect.
Quest Nutrition
Loaded Taco Tortilla-Style Protein Chips (1.1 oz bag — 140 cal / 19g protein / 4g net carbs)
The macro lever — chips that contribute 19g protein instead of zero. Turns the carb slot into a second protein slot. Baked, not fried. The whole recipe is built around this SKU on the adult side.
Kraft
Fat-Free Shredded Cheddar Cheese (1 oz per adult meal-prep container — 45 cal / 9g protein / 0g fat per oz)
The adult-side macro saver. Same melt + similar flavor as full-fat sharp cheddar, but 65 cal lower + 9g fat lower per oz. Portioned directly into each adult container so it melts through under the microwave reheat.
Velveeta
Slices (1.5 slices per shared kid container — split between two kids, ~50 cal / 3g protein per 3/4 slice)
Refresh swap for kid cheese — melts creamier than shredded cheddar under the microwave reheat and reads familiar for kids. Filmed spec: 1.5 slices per shared kid container, later split between two children.
Simply Tostitos
Regular yellow corn tortilla chips (~1 oz per kid — ~150 cal / 2g protein / 18g net carbs per oz)
Kid-side chip. Restaurant-style thin yellow corn — familiar texture kids expect. Half the cost of Quest chips ($3 bag vs $0.75/oz) — wasted spend if you give Quest to a kid.
Wholly Guacamole
Classic Minis (6-cup pack, 2 oz / cup — 100 cal / 1g protein / 8g fat per mini)
Pre-portioned guac = portion-creep killer. Refresh spec: 1/2 mini per adult (60 cal, in the 500-cal budget), 1 full mini per kid. Same SKU as id 42 carnitas — already-in-your-fridge cross-recipe ingredient.
Siete
Habanero Botana Sauce (adult-only heat drizzle — ~15 cal / 1g fat per tbsp)
Refresh addition — the adult-only heat lever. Filmed as the light sauce drizzle over the finished adult bowl. Never on the kid plate. Sub any habanero-based hot sauce (Lucky Dog, Cholula Chili Lime) — macro impact is negligible.
Romaine hearts + yellow cherry tomatoes
Cold produce — chopped romaine + halved yellow cherry tomatoes
Refresh produce swap from shredded iceberg + diced Roma. Refrigerated separately from the warm beef containers so texture holds until assembly. Yellow cherry tomatoes photograph brighter than Roma against the cheesy beef.
Kirkland Signature
Organic Chicken Sipping Bone Broth (1 tbsp per meal-prep container = 6 tbsp total, ~17 cal)
Refresh reframes the bone broth as a MOISTURE HACK per meal-prep container — 1 tbsp splashed into each container so the beef stays moist through the microwave reheat. Cross-recipe across id 4, 24, 30, 38, 39, 41, 42.
